title: When Defense Becomes Compulsion: An Evolutionary and Circuit Framework for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
title_zh: 防御成为强迫：强迫症的进化与电路框架
abstract: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is characterized by intrusive thoughts and repetitive behaviors that are frequently organized around preventing potential harm. Although existing neurobiological models have focused on abnormalities in cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical circuits, habit formation, and cognitive control, they provide a less complete explanation for why compulsions preferentially take the form of precautionary actions. Here, we propose an evolutionary and circuit-level framework in which compulsive behavior is understood as a pathological dysregulation of neural systems that normally support adaptive defense. Integrating evidence from human studies with circuit-level findings from rodent studies, we organize defensive control into three sequential but interacting stages: threat appraisal, defensive action selection and execution, and post-defense safety assessment. During threat appraisal, abnormalities in sensory salience, threat valuation, contextual gating, and interoceptive processing may increase the salience or threat value of ambiguous cues. During action selection and execution, intolerance of uncertainty, impaired behavioral flexibility, corticostriatal dysfunction, and negative reinforcement may bias behavior toward premature and repetitive threat-reducing actions that can become increasingly habitual. Following defensive action, impaired outcome evaluation and safety-state updating may prevent successful actions from generating stable signals of safety or completion, allowing defensive responding to persist despite objective threat reduction. By organizing OCD-related circuitry according to when it contributes to defensive processing rather than solely where abnormalities occur, this framework integrates threat-based, corticostriatal, habit, and safety-learning accounts into a process-based model of how adaptive defense may transition into persistent compulsive behavior. This framework may help map stage-specific dysfunction onto symptom heterogeneity and guide more targeted interventions.
abstract_zh: 强迫症（OCD）的特征是侵入性思维和重复性行为，这些行为常围绕预防潜在危害而组织。尽管现有的神经生物学模型已聚焦于皮质-纹状体-丘脑-皮质回路的异常、习惯形成和认知控制，但它们对为何倾向于以预防性行动形式出现的强迫行为提供的解释不够完整。本文提出一个进化与电路层面的框架，将强迫行为理解为神经系统正常支持适应性防御的病理性失调。整合人类研究与啮齿类研究的电路证据，我们将防御控制组织为三个顺序但相互作用的阶段：威胁评估、防御性行动选择与执行，以及防御后安全评估。在威胁评估阶段，感觉显著性、威胁价值、情境门控和本体感知的异常可能会增加模棱两可线索的显著性或威胁价值。在行动选择与执行阶段，不确定性容忍度受损、行为灵活性受损、皮质-纹状体功能障碍和负向强化可能会倾向于提前且重复的减少威胁行动，这些行动可能越来越习惯化。防御后，结果评估受损和安全状态更新受阻可能阻止成功的行动产生稳定的安全或完成信号，从而允许防御性反应尽管客观上威胁已降低却持续存在。通过根据防御处理何时贡献而非仅仅其中异常位置来组织与OCD相关的电路，本框架将基于威胁、纹状体、习惯和安全学习的各类解释整合为一个过程模型，阐述适应性防御如何转变为持续的强迫行为。该框架可能有助于将阶段特异性功能障碍映射到症状异质性，并指导更具针对性的干预措施。
